seo.meta_description: Toyota C-HR 2016-2023 import from Japan for NZ buyers. Hybrid or 1.2 turbo options, compact SUV size, and auction sourcing support.
seo.og_title: Toyota C-HR 2016-2023 Import from Japan NZ
seo.og_description: Looking at a Toyota C-HR 2016-2023? We help NZ buyers source vehicles from Japan, explain the available specs, and check import viability before bidding.

blocks.hero_subtitle: The 2016-2023 Toyota C-HR is a compact crossover that works for buyers who want SUV ride height without moving into a larger vehicle. Across this model run you can target either the 1.8 hybrid for everyday economy or the 1.2 turbo if AWD matters more.
proof_points: Japan specialists with direct auction access
Importing estimate, compliance is part of the process
blocks.why_kiwis_buy: The C-HR appeals because it is easy to place in town, but it still gives you the higher driving position many buyers want. The hybrid version is the one most people ask about, because Toyota's 1.8 petrol-electric setup is familiar, simple to live with, and well suited to commuting. For buyers worried about overpaying or ending up with the wrong variant, the key is checking the exact model code, grade and import viability before bidding.
blocks.video_caption: From the outside the C-HR sits in that useful middle ground, shorter and easier to park than a larger SUV, but with more ride height than a hatch. If the car in the video is a G or GR SPORT grade, we will confirm the exact trim and listed equipment before you bid.
blocks.main_usp_deep: The big draw with the C-HR is that Toyota gave buyers two genuinely different powertrains in the same body. ZYX11 hybrid cars use the 1.8-litre 2ZR-FXE petrol-electric setup, while NGX50 cars use the 1.2-litre 8NR-FTS turbo. That matters because you can shop the same shape around your real use, hybrid for lower day-to-day fuel spend, or turbo AWD grades such as G-T if you want extra traction. One useful detail many buyers miss is that E-Four hybrid availability was part of the model story early on, so drivetrain needs should be checked by model code and grade rather than assuming every hybrid is front-wheel drive.

buyer_persona.headline: Who is this car right for?
buyer_persona.body: This suits someone who wants a compact SUV for daily use, values Toyota hybrid familiarity, and does not need the cabin space of a RAV4 or Harrier. It also works for buyers who like the idea of AWD but do not want to jump into a much larger vehicle, as long as the exact NGX50 or hybrid drivetrain they want is confirmed before bidding. For that kind of buyer, it is a solid match.

car_specs_benefits.spec: 1.8-litre hybrid system based on the 2ZR-FXE engine, 72kW engine output
car_specs_benefits.benefit: This is the C-HR setup most buyers look for when running costs matter, especially in stop-start commuting.
The turbo option gives you a non-hybrid alternative and opens the door to AWD grades such as NGX50 G-T.

car_specs_benefits.spec: Body size around 4385-4390mm long, 1795mm wide, 1550mm high
car_specs_benefits.benefit: That footprint is easier to park and place than a mid-size SUV, while still giving the raised seating position buyers want.

car_specs_benefits.spec: Hybrid FF variants and turbo FF variants were offered, with E-Four and 4WD availability depending on version
car_specs_benefits.benefit: You are not locked into one drivetrain, so the search can be narrowed around economy or extra traction.

car_specs_benefits.spec: GR SPORT was offered later in the model run
car_specs_benefits.benefit: If you want the sharper-looking end of the range, there is a real factory sport grade to target rather than relying on aftermarket add-ons.

standout_features_block.headline: What sets it apart
standout_features_block.intro: The C-HR makes more sense when you focus on the useful equipment differences between grades, not just the shape.

items.title: Toyota Safety Sense on later high-spec cars
items.body: Later examples and special editions can include Toyota's active safety package, depending on grade and year. That is worth chasing because it bundles the driver-assist features buyers actually use, rather than cosmetic extras alone.
items.image_hint: Close view of the upper windscreen area and steering wheel controls that show the driver-assist hardware and buttons

items.title: GR SPORT factory trim
items.body: GR SPORT is not just a badge to search by. It gives buyers a factory sport-oriented version of the C-HR, which matters if you want the sharper end of the range without piecing a car together from accessories.
items.image_hint: Three-quarter cabin shot showing GR SPORT seats, steering wheel and trim details

items.title: Mode-Nero Safety Plus III special editions
items.body: These named editions are useful because they package appearance and safety equipment into one grade search. If that exact version is on your shortlist, we confirm the listed trim on the auction list rather than assuming equipment from the badge alone.
items.image_hint: Dashboard and front-seat photo showing the upgraded trim presentation of a special-edition cabin

items.title: Compact crossover packaging
items.body: The C-HR's main practical feature is its size. It gives you SUV ride height and easier entry than a hatch, without stepping up to a larger body that costs more to park and live with.
items.image_hint: Urban parking scene showing the C-HR fitting neatly into a standard parking space

tech_deep_dive_block.headline: Under the skin
tech_deep_dive_block.intro: The C-HR range is worth understanding properly because the model code tells you a lot about how the car will feel to own.

items.title: ZYX11 1.8 Hybrid
items.body: ZYX11 is the code to know if you are searching for the 1.8-litre hybrid version. It uses Toyota's petrol-electric setup based on the 2ZR-FXE 1797cc engine, with 72kW from the petrol engine. Because it is a self-charging hybrid, there is no plug to deal with and no change to how you refuel the car. The appeal is straightforward, lower fuel use in traffic and Toyota hybrid hardware that many NZ buyers already understand.

items.title: NGX50 1.2 Turbo
items.body: NGX50 is the 1.2-litre turbo C-HR, built around the 8NR-FTS 1196cc engine, rated at 85kW. This is the version to look at if you want the turbo powertrain and the AWD-linked grades listed in the requested range. It gives the C-HR a different character from the hybrid, less about electric assistance and more about a small-capacity turbo doing the work. If your shortlist includes G-T or G-T Mode-Nero Safety Plus III, this is the code and engine family behind them.

items.title: 2016-2023 production run
items.body: This model run starts in late 2016 and continues through 2023, with early cars and later facelift-era cars both appearing in the auction market. That spread matters because equipment, safety features and special editions changed through the run. If you are trying to avoid overpaying for the wrong spec, year, model code and grade need to be checked together rather than treated as interchangeable.

items.title: Grade ladder in the requested scope
items.body: Confirmed grades in the requested scope include G and G Mode-Nero Safety Plus III on ZYX11 hybrid cars, G-T and G-T Mode-Nero Safety Plus III on NGX50 turbo AWD cars, plus S GR Sport and S-T GR Sport as the factory sport grades. For most buyers chasing low running costs, the hybrid G grades are the natural starting point. If you want the sportier factory look, the GR SPORT grades are the trims to target.

models_comparison.intro: If you are comparing C-HR variants, these are the points that actually change the buying decision.

rows.notes: ZYX11 uses the 1.8 hybrid based on the 2ZR-FXE engine, while NGX50 uses the 1.2 turbo 8NR-FTS. The hybrid suits lower running-cost daily use, while the turbo suits buyers who want the AWD-linked grades in the requested range.
The requested ZYX11 grades are FWD, while the requested NGX50 grades are AWD. If extra traction matters, the model code and grade matter more than the body shape.
G and G-T grades are the straightforward picks if you want the core C-HR package. S GR Sport and S-T GR Sport are better if you want the factory sport trim and a sharper visual position in the range.

rows.attribute: Regular grades vs Mode-Nero Safety Plus III
rows.notes: Mode-Nero Safety Plus III versions are useful if you want a named special edition that groups appearance and safety equipment together. They are worth targeting when the exact trim package matters more than simply buying the cheapest C-HR.

blocks.how_to_use_iyc: Send us the C-HR year range, budget, and whether you want hybrid or turbo. We check current auction availability, explain the auction list information on suitable cars, and work out an importing estimate before any bid is placed. If the numbers and the car stack up, we handle the bidding and import process from there.

faq_block.q: Should I look for the hybrid or the 1.2 turbo C-HR?
faq_block.a: That depends on how you use the car. ZYX11 hybrid cars suit buyers focused on lower day-to-day fuel spend, while NGX50 turbo cars are the ones to look at if AWD is part of the brief.

faq_block.q: What costs make up the landed price?
faq_block.a: The main components are Vehicle cost, Japan-side costs, Shipping costs, Customs clearance, Compliance, and On-road costs. We work through those before bidding so you can see how the auction price translates to a landed figure.

faq_block.q: Can you tell me if a C-HR is typically within the entry requirements?
faq_block.a: Import viability must be checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding. Final entry certification and compliance are completed in New Zealand after arrival.

faq_block.q: How long does a C-HR import take?
faq_block.a: Timing depends on when the right car appears, the shipping schedule, and the NZ arrival process. Once you have a shortlisted vehicle, we can talk you through the current timeline around that specific purchase.

faq_block.q: What do you provide from the auction side?
faq_block.a: We translate and explain the auction list information supplied for the car, including grade, mileage, condition notes, and listed modifications where present. Photos and supporting records vary between listings, so we tell you what is confirmed and what is not.

blocks.company_positioning: ImportYourCar.co.nz is an NZ-based vehicle import service operated by Ultimate Motors Ltd. We have been helping buyers source vehicles from Japanese auctions since 2009, with support around auction access, bidding, shipping, customs clearance, and the NZ arrival process.

not_for_you_block.headline: Who this may not suit
items: If you need a large back seat or a bigger boot, a RAV4, Harrier or similar SUV will make more sense.
If you want one fixed spec across the whole range, the C-HR needs a bit more homework because drivetrain and grade differences matter.

alternatives_block.intro: The C-HR sits between a hatch and a mid-size SUV, so these are the alternatives buyers usually weigh it against.

rows.better_if: You want the same broad Toyota hybrid thinking with more focus on fuel economy and everyday commuting.
rows.tradeoff: You give up the SUV seating position and crossover shape that draw people to the C-HR.

rows.better_if: You need more rear-seat room and more luggage space for family use.
rows.tradeoff: It is a larger vehicle to park and shop for, and it moves away from the C-HR's compact footprint.

rows.better_if: You want another compact crossover option from the same auction market with a similar urban focus.
rows.tradeoff: It does not offer the same Toyota hybrid path across the requested C-HR range.

battery_health_block.headline: Hybrid battery information
battery_health_block.body: For a used hybrid, the exact battery condition cannot be assumed from the model alone. What we can do before bidding is review the auction information available for the car, explain any battery-related notes if they are present, and be clear when that information is not supplied.
checklist: Confirm whether the car is ZYX11 hybrid or NGX50 turbo
Review the auction list for any hybrid-system notes
Check whether supporting records are supplied with the listing

engine_drivetrain_block.headline: Powertrain options to consider
engine_drivetrain_block.body: Across the 2016-2023 run, the C-HR was offered with two confirmed powertrains. The hybrid side is the 1.8-litre 2ZR-FXE-based setup in ZYX11 cars, while the turbo side is the 1.2-litre 8NR-FTS in NGX50 cars. In the requested scope, that means grades such as G, G Mode-Nero Safety Plus III and S GR Sport on the hybrid side, and G-T, G-T Mode-Nero Safety Plus III and S-T GR Sport on the turbo side. If drivetrain matters, that needs to be tied back to the exact model code and grade before bidding rather than assumed from the shape alone.
